title: session.opened
description: The runner dispatched a CLI session through the EngineAdapter. Parity with the creation of an agent_sessions row in flowpilot.

job_id.description: The job the session serves. Absent or null when the session serves none (a discovery session, a turn of conversation).

node_id.description: The node of the graph the session works on. It is what allows counting attempts per node instead of per job.

engine.description: Which EngineAdapter dispatched, e.g. "claude-code". The field is the border of LLM independence.

engine_session_ref.description: The session's id in the engine's own vocabulary, captured while it runs. It is the key that makes resuming possible after a quota pause.

working_dir.description: The directory the process was started in.

prompt.description: What was asked of the session. The engine's input, not a title.

timeout_seconds.description: The wall-clock budget the session was opened with. null means the session declares no policy of its own.

silence_seconds.description: The idleness budget the session was opened with: seconds with no output at all before it is stopped. Independent of the wall clock, because it measures something else — a session can stay alive and productive for an hour, and can stall in two minutes with the process still standing. null means the session declares no policy of its own.
